//: The single source of truth for what riprap wires. Both riprap's CI and
bin/riprap verify read this file, so the checker cannot drift from the wiring.
Every command here runs from the plugin, but only session-start does its work
there. The guardrail hooks are dispatched by run-payload-hook, which execs the
real script out of the project at bin/hooks/riprap/claude/ — and exits 0 in
silence if the project never ran /riprap:install, so this plugin is inert in
repositories that do not use it.
The guardrail scripts live in the project rather than here, and that is
deliberate. They share pattern libraries with the git hooks, which run for
every developer on the team — including ones who never installed this plugin.
A library living in a version-stamped, user-scoped plugin cache would simply
be missing for half of them. One rule definition, two enforcers, both
reachable from a plain clone.
lint-example.sh is deliberately absent: it is an inert template, and wiring a
rule that never fires teaches people to ignore the wiring.
The handoff hooks are wired to three different events because no single one
covers the moment that matters. PreCompact is the only warning that context is
about to be lost, and it is the one event that cannot say anything to the model:
it can only block, and blocking a compaction that is already necessary wedges
the session. So it writes to disk, and SessionStart on `compact` is what points
the next context at what it wrote.
SessionStart matches `resume` and `fork` as well. Those are not new features —
they are two of the five documented matcher values, and omitting them meant a
resumed session received no router at all, which is the single moment a handoff
is most worth surfacing.
